problem: Existing benchmarks for LLM-powered agents assume full automation but fail to capture real-world collaborative use cases where humans and agents interact.
approach: PULSE framework combines user feedback collection, ML-based satisfaction prediction, and pseudo-label integration to efficiently evaluate human-agent interactions at scale via a web platform around OpenHands.
contribution: Demonstrates that agent design impacts developer satisfaction measurably; achieves 40% reduction in confidence intervals compared to standard A/B testing and reveals discrepancies between benchmark performance and in-the-wild results.

problem: Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) and similar optimizers are sensitive to learning rate selection, requiring expensive hyperparameter tuning.
approach: Derives adaptive Polyak-type step size schedulers tailored to SAM-style updates in both deterministic and stochastic settings.
contribution: Proves linear convergence for strongly convex and O(1/T) convergence for convex objectives; empirically achieves performance comparable to carefully tuned SAM baselines with substantially reduced tuning.

problem: Neural operators perform poorly on irregular geometries, but the cause remains unclear—whether it is merely an encoding issue or a deeper architectural limitation.
approach: Introduces the Geometric Forgetting Hypothesis: layer-wise probing reveals that neural operators progressively lose geometric fidelity as depth increases; proposes a lightweight geometry memory injection mechanism.
contribution: Demonstrates systematic geometric forgetting in both spectral and attention-based operators; shows that geometry retention improves accuracy, stability, and generalization.

problem: Multi-armed bandit algorithms for satisficing (identifying arms above a threshold) have poor regret bounds when the excess gap is small relative to suboptimality gaps.
approach: Introduces a refined regret notion and proposes uncertain-UCB algorithm that achieves pseudo-regret depending on gaps only for arms exceeding threshold.
contribution: Proves satisficing pseudo-regret of O(sum_{i:Delta_i>Delta_*} ln(K/Delta_*)/Delta_i) and establishes a near-matching lower bound.

problem: Concept erasure methods for diffusion models may only conceal harmful concepts rather than truly removing them, risking malicious exploitation.
approach: Reveals the Erasure Evasion Backdoor (EEB) attack where adversaries bind backdoors to concepts before erasure, allowing the malicious link to survive fine-tuning.
contribution: Demonstrates up to 82% success against celebrity-identity unlearning, up to 94% for object erasure, and up to 16x amplification of explicit-content exposure across six erasure methods.

problem: Reliably attributing goals to agentic systems requires both understanding observable behavior and internal representations, but no established methodology exists.
approach: Integrates behavioral evaluation (against optimal policies across varying task difficulty) with interpretability probing of internal representations and multi-step action plans.
contribution: Shows that LLM agents encode coarse spatial maps preserving task-relevant cues and that their actions are consistent with these representations; reasoning reorganizes them from spatial cues to action selection.

problem: Existing trust assessment methods for long-form LLM responses rely on expensive claim-by-claim fact-checking that is brittle for open-ended queries.
approach: Introduces semantic isotropy—angular dispersion of text embeddings on the unit sphere—as a low-cost signal requiring no labeled data, fine-tuning, or hyperparameter selection.
contribution: Demonstrates that higher semantic isotropy reliably signals lower factual consistency across samples and consistently outperforms existing aggregate trust signals using only a handful of samples.

problem: Neural network concepts may not align to individual neurons, motivating search for sparser representations, yet whether neuron-based features are fundamentally interpretable remains unclear.
approach: Develops gradient-based attribution pipeline for circuit tracing on the MLP neuron basis without requiring sparse autoencoders.
contribution: Empirically shows MLP neurons are as sparse a feature basis as SAEs; identifies circuits of ~100 neurons for subject-verb agreement and causal neurons for multi-hop reasoning without additional training costs.

problem: Score-based diffusion models assume fully specified inputs but real-world tabular data frequently contains missing values, limiting their applicability.
approach: Proposes AugMask: conditional stochastic augmentation via lightweight auxiliary models to complete inputs, combined with masked loss that restricts supervision to observed coordinates.
contribution: Connects AugMask to Rao-Blackwellized objective yielding variance-weighted sensitivity penalty; enables standard diffusion tabular generators to match or outperform specialized missing-aware baselines.

problem: Co-training combines limited real-world data with abundant surrogate data (simulation, cross-embodiment) but the mechanisms determining success remain poorly understood.
approach: Analyzes sim-and-real co-training through theory and controlled experiments, identifying structured representation alignment and importance reweighting effects.
contribution: Shows representation alignment plays primary role in downstream performance; validates effects on robot manipulation and motivates improved co-training method.

problem: Environment design for RL typically focuses on reward design; observation and action space design remains underexplored despite significant impact on learning efficiency.
approach: Proposes LOAM: leverages LLMs to construct refined observation and action spaces from raw environments, incorporating continuous racing to allocate resources to promising configurations.
contribution: Consistently outperforms handcrafted baselines in learning speed and asymptotic performance on HumanoidBench and Isaac Lab without additional training overhead.

problem: High-dimensionality of data is typically viewed as a statistical impediment, but when and how it becomes beneficial remains unclear.
approach: Distinguishes effective dimension, correlation rank, and latent intrinsic dimension via generalized Hanson-Wright inequality; shows increasing effective dimension drives blessing of dimensionality.
contribution: Proves persistence diagrams recover latent homology when effective dimension is in omega(log n); provides empirical evidence that grid-cell activity encodes isometric representations of physical space.

problem: Vision-Language Models undergoing continual learning suffer dual forgetting: catastrophic forgetting of new classes and erosion of foundational zero-shot capabilities.
approach: Proposes DFA-CIL framework with Similarity-Calibrated Retention metric and DFA-MoE method using functionally heterogeneous experts for feature alignment and plasticity.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art balance in preserving both incremental and pre-trained knowledge; SCR metric reveals hidden fragility of existing methods.

problem: Scaling agent training is limited by lack of diverse and reliable environments; collecting trajectories from realistic environments is inefficient.
approach: Proposes Agent World Model (AWM): fully synthetic environment generation pipeline creating 1,000 code-driven environments backed by databases with reliable state transitions.
contribution: Training exclusively in synthetic environments yields strong out-of-distribution generalization; enables reliable reward function design compared with LLM-simulated environments.

problem: Real-time ATE estimation in streaming data requires covariate balancing under distributional shifts and strict memory constraints.
approach: Proposes model-agnostic method based on discrepancy theory: compresses streaming data into feature coresets preserving balancing objectives; learns balancing weights via linear-time updates.
contribution: Establishes convergence guarantees with explicit memory and computational complexity bounds; consistently outperforms existing techniques on synthetic and real-world datasets.

problem: Machine learning approaches for predicting Lagrangian Relaxation multipliers lack theoretical understanding of when and how they generalize.
approach: Analyzes learning LR multipliers via data-driven algorithm design lens; derives generalization bounds and proves stochastic gradient ascent with averaging achieves minimax optimal rate.
contribution: Proves generalization bound of O(s^1.5/sqrt(N)), minimax lower bound of Omega(s/sqrt(N)), and minimax optimal rate Theta(s/sqrt(N)); extends to learning-to-warm-start with rate Theta(s/N).

problem: Fine-tuning aligned LLMs induces emergent misalignment: unexpected harmful behaviors far outside the intended domain, detectable only during deployment.
approach: Evaluates five in-training regularization interventions including KL-divergence, feature-space distance, adversarial steering, interleaving, and inoculation prompting.
contribution: Demonstrates that selecting interleaving data by perplexity gap between aligned and misaligned models yields best results overall for preventing broad misalignment.

problem: Red-teaming LLMs requires finding both effective and diverse attacks, but existing GFN methods suffer training instability and mode collapse from unstable reward functions.
approach: Proposes Stable-GFlowNet (S-GFN) eliminating Z estimation through pairwise comparisons and robust masking against noisy rewards; adds fluency stabilizer.
contribution: Provides more stable training while maintaining GFN's optimal policy; demonstrates overwhelming attack performance and diversity across various settings.

problem: Autoregressive LLM decoding requires sequential generation causing high latency and poor GPU utilization despite parallel verification via speculative decoding.
approach: Introduces DFlash: employs lightweight block diffusion model for parallel drafting in speculative decoding, conditioning draft model on context features from target model.
contribution: Achieves over 6x lossless acceleration across models and tasks; delivers up to 2.5x higher speedup than state-of-the-art speculative decoding method EAGLE-3.

problem: Conditional sampling from flow matching models requires additional training or suffers from importance weight degeneracy in high dimensions.
approach: Proposes TFTF: training-free method combining importance sampling with sequential Monte Carlo resampling during intermediate generation stages; uses stochastic flow with adjustable noise.
contribution: Requires no additional training while providing theoretical guarantees of asymptotic accuracy; significantly outperforms existing approaches on conditional sampling tasks for MNIST, CIFAR-10, and text-to-image generation.

problem: Out-of-distribution detection relying on real-valued magnitude features neglects semantic richness in phase information and lacks systematic uncertainty modeling.
approach: Proposes TrustworthyQENN bridging complex-valued representation learning with generalized quantum evidence theory; uses supervised complex-valued contrastive learning and quantum evidence generation.
contribution: Achieves peak AUROC of 95.94% on MSTAR dataset while consistently outperforming state-of-the-art methods on OOD detection across benchmarks.

problem: Understanding thermodynamic capacity limits and retrieval robustness of modern Hopfield networks with continuous states remains unclear.
approach: Derives thermodynamic phase boundaries for Dense Associative Memory networks with exponential capacity under geometric constraints; compares Gaussian and Epanechnikov kernels.
contribution: Shows maximum theoretical capacity alpha=0.5 at zero temperature; identifies qualitative differences between kernels: LSE exhibits critical line at all loads while LSR has threshold below which no spurious patterns exist.

problem: Identifying common hub variables across multiple Gaussian Graphical Models requires estimating all subpopulation GGMs, which is computationally expensive.
approach: Proposes Joint Inverse Components for Hub Detection (JIC-HD) leveraging joint minimax eigenspaces to recover common hubs without estimating full subpopulation GGMs.
contribution: Establishes theoretical guarantees for common hub recovery; outperforms existing methods especially when GGMs have both common and individual hubs; identifies biologically meaningful hub genes across cancer subtypes.

problem: Current context engineering methods rely on manually crafted, rigid heuristics that impose structural biases and restrict design space exploration.
approach: Proposes Meta Context Engineering (MCE): bi-level framework where meta-level agent refines engineering skills via agentic crossover over history of skills and executions, base-level agent optimizes context as flexible files and code.
contribution: Achieves 5.6-53.8% relative improvement over state-of-the-art agentic context engineering (mean 16.9%); maintains superior context adaptability, transferability, and efficiency.

problem: Continual learning with large pre-trained models using LoRA-based Mixture-of-Experts suffers from redundancy, interference, routing ambiguity, and forgetting from coarse-grained experts.
approach: Proposes MoRAM (Mixture of Rank-1 Associative Memory) viewing weight matrices as linear associative memories; each rank-1 adapter acts as content-addressable memory unit evaluated via intrinsic key.
contribution: Significantly outperforms state-of-the-art continual learning methods on CLIP and LLMs; achieves better plasticity-stability trade-off, stronger generalization, and reduced forgetting.

problem: Vision Transformers can be driven by spurious cues; understanding their inner workings via interpretability remains challenging due to limited concept coverage and subjective feature interpretation.
approach: Proposes ViSAE: mechanistic interpretability toolbox using sparse autoencoders with 64K probing images and 16K visually grounded concept vocabulary; includes concept reading and circuit tracing algorithms.
contribution: Improves concept coverage efficiency by 20x over ImageNet and interpretation accuracy by 28.7% over existing concept sets; concept editing improves worst-group accuracy on WaterBirds by 48.2%.

problem: Theoretical understanding of why reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) outperforms supervised fine-tuning (SFT) for reasoning remains lacking.
approach: Models chain-of-thought reasoning as pathfinding on graphs; proves SFT fails to learn efficient backtracking while RLVR learns backtracking from outcome rewards.
contribution: Demonstrates inference-time compute separation between SFT and RLVR; shows RLVR learns location of difficult decisions enabling better compute allocation; reasoning traces distill to base models for efficient backtracking.

problem: Multimodal Diffusion Transformers exhibit prompt forgetting: prompt semantics progressively degrade across text branch layers, weakening instruction-following.
approach: Proposes prompt reinjection: training-free approach reinjects prompt representations from early layers into later layers to alleviate forgetting.
contribution: Consistent improvements on GenEval, DPG, and T2I-CompBench++ in instruction-following capability and text-image generation quality across SD3, SD3.5, and FLUX.1.

problem: Fine-tuning LLMs for preference alignment via RLHF is computationally expensive and complex; Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) has limitations including hyperparameter sensitivity and GPU requirements.
approach: Proposes COALA: lightweight algorithm leveraging convex optimization reformulation of neural networks; eliminates reference model and uses single GPU training.
contribution: Competitive performance with DPO while utilizing only ~17.6% of DPO's total TFLOPs; exhibits stable monotonically increasing rewards and reaches peak margins faster than DPO and ORPO.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models benefit from Chain-of-Thought reasoning but incur high inference overhead and rely on discrete reasoning mismatching continuous perception.
approach: Proposes Latent Reasoning VLA (LaRA-VLA) internalizing multi-modal CoT into continuous latent representations; uses curriculum-based training transitioning from explicit supervision to latent reasoning.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art VLA methods while achieving up to 90% reduction in inference latency compared to explicit CoT-based VLA approaches.

problem: Current AI-generated video evaluation relies on limited metrics and datasets; assessing text-to-video generation and video-to-text interpretation at scale lacks comprehensive benchmarks.
approach: Presents AIGVE-60K dataset with 3,050 prompts across 20 task dimensions, 120K MOSs, and 60K QA pairs on 58,500 videos from 30 T2V models; proposes LOVE metric and LOVE-Reward for optimization.
contribution: LOVE achieves state-of-the-art performance on AIGV evaluation across multiple dimensions; LOVE-Reward significantly improves video generation quality via reinforcement learning.

problem: LoRA initialization critically depends on subspace selection; existing approaches using weight-only magnitude overlook task-relevant information in downstream data distribution.
approach: Proposes Fisher-guided framework leveraging downstream data curvature to identify parameter directions impacting predictions; formulates initialization as data-aware sensitivity problem.
contribution: Data-aware initialization consistently and significantly improves downstream performance across diverse tasks and modalities compared to existing approaches.

problem: Dataset condensation for diffusion models must preserve distributional geometry required by diffusion likelihood objectives, not just sample fidelity.
approach: Reformulates real subset selection as geometry-aware distribution alignment via one-sided partial optimal transport; complements with feature-statistics and semantic consistency regularization.
contribution: Achieves superior fidelity and distributional coverage in diffusion model training across diffusion variants, subset sizes, and training rounds.

problem: LLMs trained on shuffled data have frozen knowledge at training time; temporal grounding of factual knowledge and impact of data ordering remain poorly understood.
approach: Introduces benchmark of 7,000+ temporally grounded questions with evaluation protocol; pretrains 6B-parameter models on temporally ordered Common Crawl snapshots vs shuffled.
contribution: Sequentially trained models match shuffled baselines on general understanding while exhibiting more up-to-date and temporally precise knowledge; temporally ordered pretraining improves factual freshness.

problem: Video anomaly detection with multimodal LLMs requires large-scale annotations or expert-designed priors for effective anomaly knowledge acquisition.
approach: Proposes Linguistic Relative Policy Optimization (LRPO) distilling group-relative semantic advantages from reasoning trajectories into linguistically expressed anomaly experience prior.
contribution: Significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods on XD-Violence, UCF-Crime, and UBNormal under tuning-free settings via contextual experience injection without parameter updates.

problem: Standard tokenization techniques poorly handle non-stationary, multi-scale heterogeneous IoT sensing signals lacking meaningful temporal structure alignment.
approach: Proposes Dywave: dynamic tokenization using wavelet-based hierarchical decomposition, identifies meaningful temporal boundaries corresponding to semantic events, and adaptively compresses redundant intervals.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art by up to 12% accuracy while reducing input token lengths by up to 75%; exhibits improved robustness to domain shifts and varying sequence lengths.

problem: Optimal transport efficiently minimizes displacements but is sensitive to rotations; Gromov-Wasserstein addresses this but suffers non-convex optimization with cubic time complexity.
approach: Identifies broad class of distortion penalties reducing to simple alignment problem in lifted feature space; introduces iterative GW solver with linear memory and quadratic time complexity.
contribution: Scales to hundreds of thousands of points in minutes with strong theoretical guarantees; differentiable and enables exploration of GW energy landscape encoding matching symmetries.

problem: Data pricing in cloud-based AutoML marketplaces involves complex challenges; direct dataset pricing is difficult and AutoML solutions don't leverage external data.
approach: Proposes data-augmented AutoML market with pricing grounded in instrumental value—marginal model quality improvement from external datasets—accommodating diverse buyer valuations via menu options.
contribution: Provides economically sustainable framework for monetizing external data that integrates with existing cloud platforms like Google's Vertex AI.

problem: Extreme multi-label classification with millions of labels makes the output layer a memory-compute bottleneck; sparsity methods fail to yield proportional speedups due to irregular memory access.
approach: Introduces group-shared fixed fan-in sparsity where semantically related labels share sparse input patterns; decomposes output into dense head for frequent labels and sparse tail for remainder.
contribution: Achieves up to 4.4x speedup in forward pass and up to 25x in backward passes over standard fixed fan-in sparsity via custom CUDA kernels leveraging hardware primitives.

problem: Existing decentralized bi-level optimization assumes lower-level strong convexity; extending to nonconvex lower-level while avoiding artificial regularization remains open.
approach: Proposes decentralized stochastic first-order algorithm for nonconvex lower-level satisfying Polyak-Łojasiewicz condition; uses constant single-timescale learning rate.
contribution: First algorithm for nonconvex decentralized bi-level optimization with convergence guarantees under mild conditions; validated on hyperparameter optimization and model pruning.
